summary.intent: Diagnose why, after a user logs out and back in, a previously-visible subfolder in the folder tree becomes non-navigable (cold-state subfolder navigation failure), matching the known GAP-2 issue from the exit-gate triage.
summary.outcome: Traced the full resolve/publish path across the mock-ipns-routing service, the API's delegated routing calls, and the folder_ipns/ipns_records DB tables, correlating request timing with DB rows to pin down the root cause; recorded the live finding as an addendum to 68.1-VERIFICATION.md and committed it. No code fix was implemented in this session — diagnosis only.

repo: Cold-state subfolder navigation failure after logout/login corresponds to GAP-2 in the exit-gate triage SUMMARY — a previously documented, not-yet-fixed gap.
mock-ipns-routing keeps a queryable request log; resolved names can be split into 'wiped' vs 'published-this-lifetime' buckets to correlate with 404s seen after re-login.
404ing IPNS names were cross-checked for existence in folder_ipns and against republish scheduling coverage in ipns_records — pointing at a republish/enrollment gap rather than a routing bug.
Publish call chain: createFolder -> createAndPublishIpnsRecord -> client.createFolder's child publish path; ipns_records persistence happens at specific API endpoints separate from the resolve path.

code.finding: Appended a live-finding addendum documenting the GAP-2 cold-state subfolder navigation root-cause trail (mock-ipns-routing logs, folder_ipns/ipns_records correlation).

workflow: When a user-reported bug matches a previously triaged gap, check the existing diagnostic trail/SUMMARY first before re-deriving the investigation from scratch.
Cross-referencing service request logs against DB tables (with direct postgres role queries) was necessary to disambiguate 'never published' vs 'published but wiped' failure modes.

friction: Root-causing required a long sequential chain of ~18 tool calls spanning service logs, two DB tables, and multiple code paths (resolve flow, persistence endpoints, publish/enrollment chain) — no single source of truth for the bug.
Needed direct postgres role access to query folder_ipns/ipns_records rather than relying on app-level tooling.
open_items: Actual code fix for GAP-2 cold-state subfolder navigation is still unimplemented — this session only produced a diagnostic addendum in VERIFICATION.md, not a patch.
Republish/enrollment coverage gap for ipns_records (implicated in the 404s) needs a concrete remediation, not just documentation.
